plan: Baseline: tests (12) and acceptance (8) all pass.
Contracts: low_stock consumes Inventory.items() and does not mutate it (qa/test_qa.py).
Integration: add/remove/report flow with normalised SKUs.
Edge cases: non-string SKUs, None/bool/float/str qty, 10**30 quantities, threshold 0 and negative, empty inventory, failed add creates no entry, qty validation before stock check on unknown SKU.
Acceptance: the 8 ACs pass; no duplicate tests written.
Regression, non-functional: discarded (no prior code beyond the version module, no security or performance requirements).
Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s qa (9 tests, all pass). No defects found.
gaps: Concurrency is out of scope (section 2), so it was not tested.
Python 3.9 compatibility was not checked; only the local interpreter was used.

advisory.problem: AC-003 only tries invalid quantities on a SKU that already exists. It never checks that a failed add with an invalid qty leaves no entry for a new SKU, and never checks that remove with an invalid qty on an unknown SKU raises ValueError instead of InsufficientStock. The criterion's scenario is the existing SKU A at 5, so this is outside the criterion.
advisory.evidence: An implementation that checks stock before it validates qty in remove, or that creates the entry before validating in add, still passes, because the tests only use A, which has stock 5.

advisory.problem: AC-007 and AC-008 use single-letter uppercase SKUs and one threshold each. They would not catch sorting by quantity alone with a stable insertion order in AC-007. AC-008 does cover tie ordering, so this is minor.
advisory.evidence: All cases in the two tests are covered by the literals. A hardcoded return would still fail on the other test, so only a minor gap remains.
